newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices falter in sight of six-year highs.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices falter in sight of six-year highs.

text.p: Oil prices faltered in their bid to revisit six year highs on Monday and fell back heavily after a failed push to the summit.

North Sea Brent crude oil futures traded in London fell a hefty 86 cents to close at $23.50 a barrel, having earlier climbed to the day's high of $24.60 -- within sight of the $25.06 post-Gulf War high set in October last year.

While winter temperatures in key European and U.S. consumer regions have kept demand for heating oil buoyant and inventories low, traders said that oil markets were jittery at their recent high levels.
"The market has been overbought for a long time and needed a bit of a shake-out," said one broker at London's International Petroleum Exchange.

The fall in prices gathered momentum in both London and New York as technical selling stops were triggered and large investment funds switched capital from oil to other futures markets such as other commodities and equities.

Nevertheless, the extent of the sell-off surprised some market-watchers who expected forecasts of cold weather in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil consuming region, to keep a floor under prices.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp said it expected below normal temperatures at least until midweek in the Northeast U.S., followed by another cold spell later this week.
Record low inventory levels in the U.S. and Europe have also kept a flame under oil prices over recent weeks.
"With the cold weather and low stocks people have been afraid to sell, but once it started to go it really went," said one London-based futures broker.
And signs from the latest European data were that stock levels were on the rebound.
Inventories in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 13.51 million barrels in December to 1.034 billion barrels, Stichting Euroilstock said in a monthly report released on Monday.
The lean stock situation, a result of oil company tactics to slim down stockpiles to cut costs and free up capital for investments, remains key to the oil price outlook.
